_readme: Every wire Uniagent ships, as data. A wire is the SHAPE of an API - the
protocol its endpoint speaks - not the company running it, which is why
'openai' here is spoken by OpenRouter, Groq, Together, xAI, Mistral,
Fireworks, Ollama and LM Studio just as much as by OpenAI.
THIS FILE IS SHIPPED AND IS REPLACED BY AN UPDATE. Do not edit it - your
changes would be a merge conflict the next time Uniagent updates. Edit
wires.json in the project root instead: it is merged over this one key by
key, so overriding a wire's URL still lets an update fix its body template
underneath you. The settings page writes there, and 'revert' deletes from
there. See scripts/wires.py for the full format.
dialect      how the history is built and the reply is read: openai,
anthropic or gemini. The one part that is code.
endpoint     appended to the base URL. Takes placeholders.
auth         which header (or query parameter) carries the key.
body         THE REQUEST, IN ORDER. Written here is sent in that order.
$model $messages $system $temperature $tools $stop
$max_tokens $want_usage $key $setting:NAME
A placeholder with no value deletes its key, and anything
that leaves empty, outward - which is how systemInstruction
disappears whole on a turn with no system text.
models       the catalogue endpoint, and where the ids are in its reply.
fields       extra boxes this wire's settings form asks for, beyond a
base URL and a key. Saved on the provider itself, and
falling back to the environment variable of the same name.
base_url     false to hide the URL box, or a string to rename it.
key          false to hide the API key box.
native       true for a wire that is a Python function rather than a
spec, because it is not HTTP-and-JSON at all.

openai.label: OpenAI
openai.help: The /chat/completions shape, and by far the most widely spoken one - most third-party endpoints serve it, so point this at any of them and it works. Uniagent drops a parameter and retries if a model rejects it, so newer models that refuse 'stop' or a non-default temperature need no configuration.

deepseek.label: DeepSeek
deepseek.help: The OpenAI wire plus DeepSeek's own two quirks: a leading 'answer in English' system message, without which it tends to reply in Chinese, and the reasoning_content round-trip its thinking models demand on any turn that made a tool call. A DeepSeek key wants this rather than plain openai, which would fail on deepseek-reasoner.

anthropic.label: Anthropic
anthropic.help: Claude's own API. The system prompt travels in its own top-level field rather than as a message, and tool calls arrive as content blocks - both handled by the anthropic dialect.

gemini.label: Google Gemini
gemini.help: Google's own API. The model id goes in the URL rather than the body, the conversation is called 'contents', and alt=sse is what makes it stream as Server-Sent Events instead of one big JSON array at the end.

local.label: Local model server
local.help: An OpenAI-compatible server running on this machine or your network - LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp. Same wire as openai; the only difference is that it takes no key, so it doesn't ask for one. Its model list comes from the server's own /models, so whatever you have loaded is what you can pick.

bedrock.label: Amazon Bedrock
bedrock.help: Signs requests with AWS SigV4 rather than sending a key, so there is no URL to point at and no bearer token. Leave the credential boxes empty to use whatever this machine already has - ~/.aws/credentials, an instance role, or the AWS_* variables in the environment. Fill them in to give this provider its own account.

fields.label: region
fields.help: Which region's Bedrock endpoint to call. Models are enabled per region, so a model that works in one may not exist in another.

fields.label: profile
fields.help: A named profile out of ~/.aws/credentials. Use this OR the two keys below, not both - a profile wins if it is set.

fields.label: access key id
fields.help: Only needed if you are not using a profile or an instance role.

fields.label: secret access key
fields.help: The other half of the access key. Stored on this provider in .env.

fields.label: session token
fields.help: Only for temporary credentials (STS, SSO, an assumed role). Leave empty for long-lived keys.

claude-subscription.label: Claude subscription (Claude Code CLI)
claude-subscription.help: Spends the Claude subscription already signed in on this machine, through the Claude Agent SDK driving the claude CLI. There is no endpoint and no API key: sign in once with `claude login` in a terminal. It needs the SDK installed (pip install --user claude-agent-sdk) and needs to be able to FIND the CLI - which is what the path box below is for, because a background service does not get your shell's PATH.

fields.label: path to the claude CLI
fields.help: Leave empty to look on PATH. Set it if this provider says it can't find the CLI while `which claude` works in your terminal - a systemd service has a minimal PATH that usually leaves out ~/.local/bin, which is where npm and pipx put things.

fields.label: timeout (seconds)
fields.help: How long to wait for a reply before giving up. The CLI is slower to first token than an HTTP API because it starts a process per turn.
